label: DRY RUN on development traces. Does a ported published arm get charged accelerator time and KV bytes like llf does, or is its advantage a charging artefact of the E36 class.
question: seven in-scope published arms deliver 33 to 35 of 41 robot questions at 16 devices where llf delivers 9; is that real or uncharged work
verdict: REAL, NOT A CHARGING ARTEFACT. The published arms are charged MORE, not less, and all arms spend the identical capped budget.

method.charging_is_coordinator_side: costs.recall_gpu_s and costs.episodic_gpu_s are called by live2/coordinator.py at the build, recall and monitor submit paths and spend from one Budget; the ARM never charges anything, so no arm can bypass it
method.instrumentation: both cost functions wrapped to record every charge with its tokens, readiness and resulting gpu_s; KV bytes derived as tokens x HOST_BYTES_PER_TOKEN
method.cells: 16 devices, 50:50, mode A, 600 s, seeds 0 and 4, dry run

arm_choice.reason: all are IN CARD SCOPE for C-mixed; no OUT_OF_CARD_SCOPE arm was used, since its number would not be evidence about that system anyway

headline_seed4.ratio: mooncake delivers 3.8x llf robots on 2.52x the recall accelerator time and the identical 600.0 s spent budget

mechanism.llf: readiness mix COLD 13, GPU-WARM 40 over 53 recall events at median 0.4162 gpu_s: it chains small piece builds then answers warm
mechanism.published: readiness mix COLD 37 over 37 events at median 2.1069 gpu_s: one full cold request per question
mechanism.reading: the published arms pay about 5x per event and 2.5x in total for recall, and still deliver 3.8x the robots, because a single cold answer lands inside the 5 s deadline while a chain of piece builds does not

e36_class_check.hypothesis: a ported arm whose rebuilds are not charged accelerator time or KV bytes would deliver impossibly well and look perfectly legal
evidence: every recall charge goes through the same costs.recall_gpu_s with the same COLD rate
published arms record MORE recall gpu_s than llf (79.5 against 31.6 at seed 4)
published arms request MORE total than llf (890.5 against 654.0) and are refused the excess
all arms spend the identical capped budget of 600.0 s, so delivery is compared at equal charged accelerator time

erratum.what: my first pass reported 0 robots on time for EVERY arm at both seeds
erratum.cause: I read `on_time` at the top level of outcomes.jsonl, but it is nested inside `cloud_payload`; the top-level field is always None
erratum.effect: the zeros were my own instrumentation artefact and would have hidden the real result entirely
erratum.corrected: recomputed from cloud_payload.on_time, which also reproduces the reported llf figure of 9 of 41 at seed 4 exactly

_provenance.script: scratchpad cost-check harness wrapping costs.*_gpu_s; no repo code changed
